draft.reason: Itchy blistery rash on both forearms after poison ivy contact while clearing brush Saturday, spreading a bit within that area; fever and trouble breathing are denied by report. This pattern fits allergic contact dermatitis that guidance plus an action-based safety net can cover; no decision-critical need for clinician assessment or prescribing is established on the reported facts. Distribution elsewhere, pain, pus and warmth were not reported and remain unknown.
draft.patientMessage: Self-care is reasonable now: ask your pharmacist about over-the-counter itch relief and keep the area clean. This looks like a poison ivy contact rash. Message this thread for Counsel clinician review if the rash keeps spreading, involves your face, eyes or genitals, or becomes painful, warm or draining pus, or if you develop a fever. If you get swelling of the lips, tongue or throat or trouble breathing, call 911.
differential: Allergic contact dermatitis from urushiol (poison ivy) exposure involving both forearms
More extensive or severe contact dermatitis — distribution beyond the forearms not reported
Secondary bacterial skin infection — pain, warmth, pus not reported and not excluded

redFlags.quote: spreading a bit within that area

redFlags.concern: Involvement of face, genitals or eyes

draft.vitalSigns: No vital-sign values reported. Whether temperature or other vital signs were measured is unknown; fever is denied as a symptom only, which does not establish any measurement.
draft.evidenceLimitations: Consumer summaries support general poison ivy rash description and when to contact a provider; the contact dermatitis synthesis is an agent-compiled emergency-department reference, not a telehealth protocol, and its severity thresholds (e.g., BSA extent, face/genital involvement) cannot be confirmed here because total body distribution was not reported. Routing rests on the patient's reported findings.

Unreported distribution and infection findings remain unknown rather than being treated as absent.

criteria.reason: The supplied consumer passages support the contact-rash inference, pharmacist-directed OTC advice and provider assessment for infection signs or fever. These changes should prompt timely clinical assessment regardless of messaging availability.

judge.correction: Retain self-care for the current presentation. In patientMessage, specify prompt same-day clinical assessment for fever, infection signs or sensitive-site involvement, and advise an appropriate local service if timely Counsel review cannot be obtained rather than waiting for a thread response.
